2. Respondent No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1002 to 1005 of 1969, in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Tangail, for correction of rights under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The case of respondent No. 1 was that the case land originally-belonged to Anath Bandhu Guna who died leaving four sons, namely, Akhil Sandhu Guha, Amar Bandhu Guha, Anil Bandhu Guha and Aghar Bandhu Guha as heirs and while the said heirs were owning and possessing the, land they, settled the same with respondent, No. 1 in 1353 B.S. by granting Pattannamas and realising rent by granting dakhilas. Further case of the plaintiff respondent was that the revisional record-of-right was wrongly prepared in the name of the said four sons of Anath Sandhu Guha overlooking the possession of the plaintiff on the basis of the settlement from the owners. The present appellant was made opposite, party No. 7 in the aforesaid Miscellaneous cases, and he contested the cases by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the documents relied upon by the plaintiff were not genuine; that after the death, of Anath Bandhu Guha the land belonged to his four sons who left for India long before, and the case land vested ill the Custodian of Enemy Property. The learned Munsif allowed the Miscellaneous Cases and directed the correction of the Khatians, holding, inter alia, that the pattannamas Exts. 1 to 1 (b) and the Dakhilas Exts. 2 to 2(g) are genuine and that respondent had been in possession of the properties. On appeal by the present-appellant the learned Subordinate Judge, Tangail, set aside the judgment of the learned Munsif on the finding that the materials produced by the plaintiff were not sufficient for corning to the finding on the case land, He further held that complicated question of title was involved in the matter and that the question of possession was not a material issue in the present case. 

 3. The respondent then filed revisional applications before the High Court Division challenging the aforesaid judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge and obtained Rules. A Single Judge of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order reversed the decisions of the lower Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court, holding, inter alia, that section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, is meant for, rectification of mistake in the entry of record-of-right and that the incidental reference to the plaintiff's title did not convert the proceeding into a title suit. The learned Judge further held that there was no, complicated question of title involved in the instant cases. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider as to whether the rectification of record-of-rights as contemplated under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, would be allowed in a case, where the plaintiff's possession in the land in question is based Oil, unregistered Pattannamas and Dhakhilas claimed by the plaintiff to have been granted by owners thereof. 

 5. Mr. Moksudor Rahman, learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellant argues that in view of the, clear finding of the Court of appeal below that a complicated question of title has arisen in the case, which cannot be decided in a summary proceeding as under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the learned Judge of the High Court Division on misinterpretation of the scope of section 143A reversed the decision of the lower appellate Court and allowed the Miscellaneous Cases.

 8. In the instant case the Circle Officer (Rev), submitted a report finding possession with the plaintiff. It is true that on an earlier occasion on 1969 the Circle Officer stated that possession was taken by the Government treating the Property as vested property. The learned trial Court however could not place any reliance on the earlier report on valid reason and relying on the later report along with the evidence, allowed the Miscellaneous Cases.
